title: RunStartParams

append_system_prompt.description: Text appended to Claude Code's system prompt (`--append-system-prompt`).

deadline_ms.description:
How long the gate waits for the app's answer to each tool call, in milliseconds
(5.1). The hook's own timeout is this plus 10 s.

mount.description: Which tools the run may reach.

needs_connectors.description:
The connectors that must be `connected` before the first turn (5.5). Not yet
served: a non-empty list is refused with `not_implemented`.

needs_you_when.description: When the finished run is `needs_you` rather than `done`.

output_schema.description:
A JSON Schema the final output must match (`--json-schema`); `run.done` then
carries `structured_output`.

partial.description:
Stream partial text as it comes (`--include-partial-messages`): `run.text` events
with `partial: true`.

persist_session.description:
Whether Claude Code keeps the session, so the run can be resumed. Absent: `true`
for a `task`, `false` for every other kind (`--no-session-persistence`).

pinned_call.description: The one call a `send_executor` or `watch` run may make. `null` is none.

prompt.description: The prompt, sent as the run's first stream-json user message.

run_id.description:
The run's id, which the app picks: a lower-case UUID, also Claude Code's session
id.

space.description: The space the run works in (`space.ensure`). Absent: `default`.

timeout_s.description:
End the run `failed {reason: "timeout"}` once its process has run this many
seconds. Absent: no limit.

Mount.description:
Which tools a run may reach (7.5).

- `{"kind": "no_tools"}`: none. rlxd passes `--tools "" --strict-mcp-config`, so
  neither built-in tools nor connectors are mounted.
- `{"kind": "connectors", "connectors": ["claude.ai Slack"]}`: built-in tools are
  dropped (`--tools ""`); the gate (5.1) decides which connector tools may be called.

oneOf.description: Only these connectors' tools, each call decided by the gate.

connectors.description:
The connectors, by the name `system/init` gives them, such as `claude.ai
Slack`.

NeedsYouWhen.description:
When a finished run is `needs_you` rather than `done` (7.5): its final output, read at
`pointer`, equals `equals`. The question is read at `question_pointer`. The output is
`structured_output` when the run has one, else the result's text read as JSON.

equals.description: The value there that means the run needs the user.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer (RFC 6901) into the output, such as `/status`.

question_pointer.description: A JSON pointer to the question to show, such as `/question`.

PinnedCall.description: The one call a `send_executor` or `watch` run may make (5.1).

input_sha256.description: The SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of the call's input as RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

RunKind.description:
What a run is for (7.5). Each kind has its own pool, and rlxd's gate rules for it
(5.1).

oneOf.description: A task the user asked for. The only kind whose session persists by default.
Sends one pinned call. Never resumed: a send is never retried.
One pinned read call for a scheduled watch.
